This is mostly down to opinion, but let's look at the bare facts regarding the actual power of each console.

The Super Nintendo (SNES) can output a total of 32,768 colours, with 256 loaded in to the usable palette at any one time.
The Mega Drive/Genesis (MDG) can output a total of 512 colours, with 61 loaded in to the usable palette at any one time.
The SNES CPU clocks at 3.58Mhz while the MDG CPU clocks at 7.67Mhz.
The SNES has 128KB RAM while the MDG has 64KB RAM.
The SNES outputs from 256x244 to 512x448 resolution, while the MDG only outputs at 320x224.
Maximum sprite sizes are 64x64 on SNES and 32x32 on MDG. Maximum number of sprites on screen at one time are 128 on SNES and 80 on MDG.
The SNES has 64KB of sound RAM and 8 channel stereo. The MDG has 8KB of sound RAM and 6 channel stereo.However, the MDG has a built-in synthesizer. It should be noted that the quality of the MDG audio varies wildly depending on which model hardware you are using.
The MDG has four graphical layers (two background, one sprite, one window). The SNES is more complicated, with 4 layers that can be used however the developer wants, up to and including Mode 7 for cheap and easy 3D effects.

I had to refresh my memory on these specs and I took them from here.

The basic hardware details are largely in favour of the SNES, with it winning every category except CPU clock-speed and lacking the MDG's synthesizer. This has been a common theme for Nintendo throughout their entire gaming history. They call it "lateral thinking with withered technology".

It should also be mentioned that the MDG's fabled "Blast Processing" is a marketing gimmick, a fancy name for absolutely nothing, and does not actually exist.

Now, when it comes to actual games, the two consoles have different libraries. Even multiplatform games (and licensed games like the Jurassic Park titles) are largely different, like the (in)famous example of Mortal Kombat with the SNES version not having any blood. In the sequel, bloody content being equal, the SNES version is superior, with a better resolution and higher quality sprites and colours, not to mention the superior (default) controller.

The SNES controller, by default, has more buttons, enabling more "complex" controls from the get-go. The MDG, on the other hand, suffered from fractured install base, since developers could not be sure which controller the user would have. This left the MDG versions of other games, like ports of four button SNK games, with problems.

The MDG also had some accessories, the Sega CD and the 32X. These rather expensive add-ons had limited libraries but, admittedly, what they did have was often quite good (not counting the 32X Doom soundtrack...). The SNES, on the other hand, did not use similar accessories but did have a SuperFX chip, a supplemental CPU, that could be included on each cartridge as needed for titles like Starfox, Vector, and Yoshi's Island.

But it all comes down to the library. The SNES, IMO, had the better library. The arcade ports were often superior thanks to a better original controller and better technical abilities, and the number of genre-defining titles on the SNES is greater than on the MDG. Games like Super Metroid, A Link to the Past, Super Mario World, Street Fighter 2 Turbo, Super Mario Kart, Starfox, Pilotwings, there were many games on the SNES that were the pinnacle of their genre for that hardware generation, and in some cases created the genre outright (i.e. the mascot racer which, thanks to Mode 7, would not have been possible on the MDG).

I'm not saying the MDG is crap, both are good and I admit to a bias in favour of Nintendo, but IMO the SNES library stands the ravages of time better than the MDG does and its technical capabilities (and forward-thinking eight button plus d-pad controller) give it a leg-up over what Sega had to offer.

If you're looking for sequels to older games, SNES. However, Genesis has much a better library of non-sequel titles. I can't think of very many great SNES games that weren't sequels (the only ones I can think of off the top of my head are Star Fox and Chrono Trigger.)
